title: Tax audit checks
learn: What a tax auditor checks on cash, TDS and late dues
Why the day an asset is first used decides depreciation
Where each finding goes in the new Form 26

Rebuild the plant and machinery block

messages: Tamhini’s tax audit, tax year 2026–27: their first on the new Form 26. I’ve picked eight items. For each, tell me what goes in the report and what it does to taxable income.
The return is due on 31 October 2027, and several of these turn on that date. Notes by Wednesday, please; Sudha reads them before she signs.

tasks.title: Check the eight items
tasks.prompt: Open each item with its papers; the audit adjustments are under Other papers. Decide what goes in the report, why, and what it adds to taxable income. Tax year 2026–27 is the first under the 2025 Act. Your calls go to Kunal when you move on.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your calls on the eight items to Kunal?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Kunal. You can read your calls but not change them.

hints: The tests: cash, per person per day (₹35,000 for goods carriages); TDS, deducted in the year and paid by 31 October 2027; employees’ PF and leave encashment, credited or paid by then; a machine, its first day of use; stock, the issue slips.

Item by item, the paper that decides it: 1, the two memos’ date and shop; 2, the gate register; 3, the TDS register; 4, the challans’ dates; 5, the PF receipt; 6, HR’s mail; 7, the commissioning report; 8, the stock summary.

fields.label: Why, and where it goes in Form 26

options.label: Paid in cash above the day limit (clause 30)
TDS not deducted in the year (clause 51(a))
Not paid by the return due date (clause 32(a))
Asset not used in the year (clause 36)
Paid to a director or relative (clause 29)

fields.label: Your note for the file
fields.placeholder: For example: bill of 12 March, paid by NEFT on 19 March

items.label: Item 1 · Cash to a hardware shop
items.prompt: Cash paid to Bhamchandra Hardware for machine-guard material. Is any of it disallowed?
items.note: Item 1: two memos, one shop, one day: ₹11,800 in cash. The limit runs per person per day, so all ₹11,800 is disallowed, though each memo is under ₹10,000. Topping up petty cash by cheque doesn’t help either. Clause 30, Yes.

items.label: Item 2 · Cash for a tempo
items.prompt: Cash paid to a tempo driver for an urgent delivery. Is any of it disallowed?
items.note: Item 2: Fine. The tempo was hired to carry goods, and for hiring a goods carriage the cash limit is ₹35,000, not ₹10,000. ₹14,500 is inside it, so nothing goes in clause 30.

items.label: Item 3 · Consultant’s fee
items.prompt: Parag Mahajani’s fee for a lean manufacturing study. Was TDS deducted, and does it matter?
items.note: Item 3: a ₹75,000 fee crosses the ₹50,000 line, so TDS was due, and none was deducted in the year. 30% is disallowed now: ₹22,500, allowed back in the year the tax is paid. “He wanted the full ₹75,000” changes nothing. Clause 51(a).

items.label: Item 4 · December TDS
items.prompt: December’s TDS: was it deposited on time, and does that cost any of December’s expenses? The interest itself is for Kunal’s computation.
items.note: Item 4: December’s TDS went in on 11 January, four days after the 7th, but long before 31 October 2027, so none of December’s expenses is disallowed. Clause 50(c) reports the interest paid: ₹6,919 with these challans and ₹8,388 on 22 January for short deductions.

items.label: Item 5 · September PF
items.prompt: September’s employees’ PF. Varun, our second-year article, has marked it on the register.
items.note: Item 5: Fine. September’s employees’ PF was credited on 27 October 2026, well before the return due date of 31 October 2027, and that date is the test from tax year 2026–27. Varun used last year’s rule: late meant lost. Clause 27(b) is No.

items.label: Item 6 · Leave encashment
items.prompt: The leave encashment provision. Earlier years’ provisions were added back in those years’ returns.
items.note: Item 6: leave encashment counts only when paid. This year’s ₹10,80,000 is unpaid, and none of it will be paid by 31 October: clause 32(a), ₹10,80,000. The ₹4,60,000 paid in March, out of earlier provisions, is allowed now. Net add-back ₹6,20,000.

items.label: Item 7 · VMC-10 in the block
items.prompt: Pallavi’s draft depreciation working puts the VMC in this year’s half-rate additions.
items.note: Item 7: the VMC reached Chakan on 24 March but was first used on 9 April. No use in the year, no depreciation: ₹54,60,000 × 7.5% = ₹4,09,500 comes out of the claim. It joins next year’s block. Clause 36.

items.label: Item 8 · Bearings 6205-2RS
items.prompt: Pallavi’s draft quantitative details: check the bearing row against the stock summary and the count.
items.note: Item 8: 21,300 bearings went out on issue slips; the draft says 21,550 consumed. The other 250 are the count shortage, hidden in consumption. They go in the shortage column. A blank there is a wrong answer, not a safe one.

tasks.title: Rebuild the plant and machinery block
tasks.prompt: Pallavi made her working from the asset register before the audit adjustments. Rebuild the 15% block from the register as it now stands, in the clause 36 lines: split this year’s additions by days of use, then work out the depreciation and the closing value.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your depreciation working to Kunal?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change it after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Kunal. You can read your working but not change it.

hints: Days of use run from the put-to-use date to 31 March. Under 180 days: half of 15%. Not used at all: not in this year’s block.
tasks.note: Line numbers follow the clause 36 schedule of Form 26. Nothing from this year’s additions was sold, so line 9 equals line 7. Lines 12–14 stay empty: under the 22% option Tamhini gets no additional depreciation.

notes.r4.amt: Sedan from 6 June (299 days) and CNC from 12 August (232 days). Pallavi’s draft starts the CNC on 1 October: still 182 days. The laptops are computers (40%) and the shed a building.
notes.r7.amt: CMM from 5 January (86 days) and the compressor from 17 January (74 days), now capitalised. The VMC was first used on 9 April 2027, so it waits for next year’s block.
notes.rx.amt: Her line 15 less the right one. Two assets make the whole difference: the VMC not used in the year, and the compressor the audit capitalised.

tasks.title: Write the points mail to Mahesh
tasks.prompt: Kunal wants one mail to Mahesh Kadam, the accounts head, with the points from your checks that need his action or his attention. Pick the right line for each point.
hints: Give Mahesh the figure from the papers and the rule that decides it. Ask him to act only where something must be fixed.

options.text: Cash payments: the ₹11,800 to Bhamchandra Hardware on 22 December and the ₹14,500 tempo of 3 February were each over ₹10,000 in a day, so both are disallowed, ₹26,300 in all. Please pay such bills by bank transfer.
options.why: Only the hardware bill. For hiring a goods carriage the limit is ₹35,000, and the tempo’s ₹14,500 is inside it.

options.text: Cash payments: the ₹11,800 to Bhamchandra Hardware on 22 December and the ₹14,500 tempo of 3 February are both allowed, as petty cash was topped up from the bank by cheque the same day.
options.why: The cheque only refilled the cash box. The shop was paid in cash, so its ₹11,800 is disallowed.

options.text: Cash payments: the ₹11,800 to Bhamchandra Hardware on 22 December is disallowed; the ₹14,500 tempo of 3 February is not, as hiring a goods carriage has a ₹35,000 limit. Please pay such bills by bank transfer.
options.why: The hardware bill is over the day limit, the tempo inside the goods-carriage limit. The last line stops a repeat.

options.text: Parag Mahajani’s bill PM/26-27/09 (₹75,000): no TDS was deducted in 2026–27, so the whole ₹75,000 is disallowed for good. Recovering the TDS from his August bill will not make any part of the fee allowable.
options.why: Too far. For a resident payee it is 30% of the fee, not all of it, and it is allowed again in the year the tax is paid.

options.text: Parag Mahajani’s bill PM/26-27/09 (₹75,000): no TDS was deducted in 2026–27, so 30% of the fee, ₹22,500, is disallowed this year. Please deduct the TDS from his August bill and deposit it with interest.
options.why: The ₹22,500 comes back in the year the tax is paid, so the fix is to deduct and deposit, with interest.

options.text: Parag Mahajani’s bill PM/26-27/09 (₹75,000): no TDS was deducted, but the fee was paid by NEFT, so nothing is disallowed. Please recover the TDS from him whenever he next bills you and deposit it.
options.why: Paying by bank does not cure a missed deduction. TDS not deducted in the year means 30% of the fee is disallowed this year.

options.text: September PF: the employees’ share of ₹3,22,829 was credited on 27 October 2026, twelve days after your register’s due date, so it is lost for good, as it was last year. It goes in the report as disallowed.
options.why: That was the rule up to 2025–26. From tax year 2026–27, crediting it by the return due date is enough.

options.text: September PF: the employees’ share of ₹3,22,829 was credited on 27 October 2026, twelve days after your register’s due date, so it is disallowed this year and allowed next year.
options.why: Employees’ PF has no later year. Credited by the return due date, it is allowed; credited after it, it is not allowed at all.

options.text: September PF: the employees’ share of ₹3,22,829 was credited on 27 October 2026, twelve days after your register’s due date but long before 31 October 2027. For tax year 2026–27 it is allowed.
options.why: Under the 2025 Act as amended in 2026, the test for employees’ PF is the return due date. The delay against Tamhini’s own register does not change the tax answer.

options.text: Depreciation: the VMC was first used on 9 April 2027, so it moves to next year’s block. The compressor, capitalised in the audit and running from 17 January, goes in at half rate.
options.why: Depreciation follows use: no use in the year, no depreciation; under 180 days of use, half the rate.

options.text: Depreciation: the VMC was billed on 22 March and reached Chakan on 24 March, so it stays in this year’s block at half rate. The compressor stays out, as it was first booked to repairs.
options.why: Arrival is not use. And the audit capitalised the compressor, so the block must have it.

options.text: Depreciation: the VMC and the compressor both reached Chakan before 31 March, so both go into this year’s block at the full 15%, counted from the dates on their purchase bills.
options.why: Full rate needs 180 days of use in the year. The compressor ran 74 days; the VMC was not used before 31 March.

options.text: Quantitative details: the 250 bearings (6205-2RS) short at the count can stay inside consumption, since the closing figure of 2,150 already agrees with the count.
options.why: The closing figure agreeing is what hides it. The schedule has a shortage column, and 250 belongs there.

options.text: Quantitative details: the 250 bearings (6205-2RS) short at the count go in the shortage column; consumption becomes the 21,300 issued on slips, not 21,550.
options.why: The shortage is shown on its own, where a reader of the report can see it.

options.text: Quantitative details: the 250 bearings (6205-2RS) short at the count should be added to taxable income, since no issue slip or other paper supports them.
options.why: The shortage is already in the accounts as a loss. The schedule reports it; nothing is added back.

principles: Read the test before the amount: a day and a person for cash, the year of deduction for TDS, the day of first use for depreciation.
A late payment is not always a disallowance, and a blank column is not always safe.
Know which Act the year falls under: tax year 2026–27 is the first under the 2025 Act, and the employees’ PF test changed with it.

interview.q: What is a tax audit, and when does a company need one?
interview.checking: Whether you know the tax audit as it is now, under the 2025 Act.
outline: A CA’s audit of the books under section 63 of the 2025 Act, before the return is filed.
Needed above ₹1 crore of business turnover; ₹10 crore if cash receipts and payments are each within 5%.
From tax year 2026–27 it is one form, Form 26; earlier years used Forms 3CA/3CB with 3CD.

interview.q: Your line says you checked tax-audit items. Which ones, and what did you find?
interview.checking: Whether the line is real and you can back it with figures.
outline: In the simulation I checked {items} items: cash, TDS, PF, leave encashment, depreciation and stock.
₹75,000 paid with no TDS: 30% of the fee, ₹22,500, is disallowed until the tax is paid.
₹14,500 cash for a tempo looked over the limit, but goods carriages get ₹35,000: allowed.
